title: Monk on acting crazy; Bud Powell, Bird and Paul Chambers
summary: Monk's remark at Birdland that they should not fall in love with the act; Chambers feigned addiction.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Bud Powell, I remember when I -- in the early '50s, I never was quite sure whether he was putting people on that he was not quite there, or whether he was not quite there, and sometimes I wonder if he knew the difference.

Well, Monk told Bud that same night that you were talking about at Birdland, when Charlie Parker was there, he walked over to the table that the both of them and says, I told you guys to act crazy, if you act crazy and get a lot of attention, but I didn't tell you to fall in love with the act. You're really crazy now.
He said that to both Parker and Powell?
The last weeks before Bird died. He said, I told you to act crazy and get attention like that, but I didn't tell you to fall in love with the act.
Did either of them respond to that?
Monk's another one who was hard to figure. Now that you say that, maybe it makes some sense, that some of his may have been an act through the years, but --
What's that bass player that started acting like a junkie and he wasn't a junkie? Came from Detroit?
No, he wasn't a junkie. He may become one later on, but he'd nod when he wasn't --
What was the point of that?
To get people to talk about you.
Strange. When did you try to act like that? I don't remember that.
